issues: The claim that decorating a function with `@weave.op` automatically creates agent conversations and turns, with no agent-specific instrumentation needed, is not supported. The evidence points the other way. S1 describes agent tracing as a separate SDK workflow: conversations, turns, LLM calls and tool calls each emit OTel spans tagged with GenAI attributes such as `gen_ai.agent.name` and `gen_ai.conversation.id`. S1 also sends readers who trace individual functions with `@weave.op` to a different page. S2 says that with agent SDK integrations, your code decides which turns belong to the same conversation, and that `weave.init()` alone isn't enough. Remove the claim. Replace it with supported guidance: use a built-in integration (S2), the Weave agent tracing helpers (S1/S4), or GenAI-tagged OTel spans (S4).

The partial answer doesn't make clear that it never explains what `@weave.op` records. It only says the setup steps are missing. The Trace LLM applications / tracing page (guides/tracking/tracing) was never read, so no claim about what `@weave.op` records can be cited yet. Read that page before answering this part.
